citation: The Chicago Blue Book of Selected Names of Chicago and Suburban Towns, for the year ending 1910. Chicago: The Chicago Directory Company.
author: The Chicago Directory Company
describes_date: 1910 (the edition 'for the year ending 1910', compiled the winter before)
locator: The classified business list, 'Livery and Boarding Stables': 'WEST GEO. G. LIVERY CO. 2123, 2125, 2127, and 2129 Indiana av. tels. Calumet-405 and 406'. For 216 E. 20th (T-3154): 'Kidde Regnar. 216 E. 20th.' and 'Willing E. A. Miss, 216 E 2oth', the first households the series seats there; Kavanagh Marcus Judge at the Congress hotel.
rights_note: A United States publication of 1910; public domain.
access_notes: Read for T-3013 on 2026-10-23 from the item's OCR text (chicagobluebooko1910chic_djvu.txt), found by the Internet Archive's full-text search; the OCR is clean in these lines.
note: The same four numbers under a new keeper, still a horse livery, on a telephone line numbered 405 as Bane Brothers' was in 1904 (South-405 then, Calumet-405 now); that it is the same line is a reading of the number, not a record of the exchange.
what_it_supplies: that 2123-2129 Indiana Avenue were still one livery in 1910, under George G. West
the first Blue Book households at 216 East 20th Street, in 1910
what_it_does_not_supply: the building's form, storeys, material or outline
